<reason>PRO won by reframing consent as ex post vs ex ante. CON's durability and equity case depended on Edinburgh/Manchester non-implementations and treating Stockholm's trial-plus-vote as CON sequencing, but PRO showed those never tested repeal, that London/Stockholm/NY survived after imposition, that worst jams make prior driver approval impossible, and that time-taxes on bus riders outweigh cash-tolls with discounts and revenue for transit. CON never answered the veto trap.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's reply that Edinburgh/Manchester never priced so prove nothing about repeal, paired with Stockholm as impose-trial-then-keep and the veto logic that worst congestion becomes unfixable if driver approval is precondition.</best_rebuttal>
